configuration_boundary.actuation_route: LowCmd joint-level control synthesized by AutoAdapter capabilities
configuration_boundary.source_interpretation: Official high-level examples establish task concepts only. The General Demo must synthesize behavior through the admitted low-level SDK route.

source_registry.basis: Official examples expose stand/lie, velocity movement, balance-attitude, trajectory-following, and special-motion task concepts.
Official Go2 interface names stand, sit, stop, recovery, Euler attitude, planar move, and gait behaviors; these are provenance, not admitted simulator calls.
Official LowCmd/LowState example demonstrates that Go2 posture behavior can be driven through the low-level route.
Official Go2 environment defines planar linear/yaw velocity commands, standing cases, disturbance pushes, and contact/orientation termination.

difficulty_policy: No Go2 difficulty label is admitted yet. The human-readable rationale is retained for later review without assigning a level.

tasks.description: Stand up from the specified supported starting posture and hold a stable upright stance.
tasks.difficulty_rationale: A single posture transition with a stationary terminal state.

tasks.description: Sit down from a stable standing posture and hold the supported sitting posture without falling.
tasks.difficulty_rationale: A controlled lowering transition with a stationary terminal state.

tasks.description: Maintain a stable upright stance at the current location for the requested interval.
tasks.difficulty_rationale: Stationary posture maintenance without a commanded displacement.

tasks.description: Move forward in the robot's initial heading direction, then stop in a stable upright stance.
tasks.difficulty_rationale: One straight translation followed by a controlled stop.

tasks.description: Adjust the robot body to the specified target height and hold it upright at the current location.
tasks.difficulty_rationale: Requires coordinated whole-body posture adjustment while constraining orientation and drift.
